notes: The wiring diagram image was not provided, so the wiring follows the manual text. The OLED and the DHT11 are powered from 3.3V. The OLED uses I2C and the DHT11 data pin goes to D4.
On the Nano form factor the I2C pins SDA and SCL are A4 and A5, so wire4 goes to A4 (SDA) and wire3 goes to A5 (SCL).
The OLED header sits in breadboard columns 10-13 (GND, VCC, SCL, SDA) and the DHT11 in columns 20-23 (VCC, DATA, NC, GND). These column positions are assumed.
The Nano Matter is wired to the breadboard with jumper wires. In the thumbnail it appears to sit on the board, but the manual doesn't say which holes it uses.
The DHT11 NC pin is only inserted into the breadboard and has no electrical connection. DHT11 is a new type because lookup_part found no match.
The Google Nest Hub Max (Thread border router) is a network device, so it is not a node in the circuit.
